title: Compact multi-language shim pattern for progressive tool responses and structured events
creator: Anya Patel
description: Goal: introduce a compact, language-idiomatic shim that standardizes progressive tool/function responses and structured event emission across TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs. Motivation: existing streaming+tool guidance is fragmented (varied framing envelopes, heavy typed adapters). This ticket proposes a minimal envelope and ergonomic bindings per language to reduce client boilerplate, ease migration, and improve binary-size/latency for mobile/edge clients. Key ideas: 1) single-byte frame start + proto-lite event payload (JSON or CBOR) to reduce header overhead; 2) a small event type registry ("delta", "tool-call", "tool-result", "error", "done"); 3) language shims that expose an async iterator (TS), generator-based iterator (Py), and channel-like consumer (Go) with the same semantic events; 4) opt-in schema validation using JSON Schema/Vanilla validators for structured outputs; 5) backward-compat fallback: server will emit both legacy framed-json and new compact frames during rollout.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped to SDK surface only (ts/py/go) — runtime and wire changes will be coordinated with serving team. Initial design doc posted (link_to_design).

2025-02-13 - Design review: PM and DX requested stronger ergonomics for TypeScript (async iterator + readable stream wrapper) and a small helper to coerce legacy tool transcripts into the new event stream. Action: add example wrappers and migration guide.

2025-02-15 - Engineering sync: agreed to use CBOR as optional compact serialization and plain JSON for human-friendliness. Decision: default to JSON over compact frames; CBOR behind a flag for Dedicated/Private where bandwidth matters.

2025-02-16 - Trade-offs logged: binary frame header reduces tokenization overhead but complicates web SDKs (WebSocket/Fetch streams). Plan: maintain text-safe base framing for browsers and provide binary mode for native SDKs.
2025-02-17 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/4125 contains preliminary TS/Py/Go shims and unit tests for framing + schema validation.
2025-02-18 - Review feedback: add typed TS definitions for structured outputs and a lightweight codegen hint for Py dataclasses. Also include an API to register custom tool event parsers in Go.

2025-02-19 - Performance note: microbenchmarks show <3% additional per-token CPU for JSON framing in Node vs previous framed-json ribbon. CBOR mode reduced payload sizes by ~22% for typical tool calls.

2025-02-20 - QA plan: end-to-end tests against runtime mock, backwards compatibility tests that assert dual-mode stream, and interop test matrix documented in the PR. Next: finalize ergonomics and begin staged rollout behind SDK flag.
Open questions: how to best signal schema evolution in long-running sessions (versioned event headers vs per-event metadata)? Proposal: per-event 'schema_version' string — requires server support.
Next steps: finalize TS helper API, add Go channel example for tool streaming consumer, write migration guide and changelog, coordinate runtime rollout with infra (feature flag).
migration_notes: Migration approach: 1) ship language shims that can decode both 'legacy-framed-json' and 'compact-frame' formats; 2) provide a dev-mode SDK flag 'redwood.experimental.compactStreaming' default=false; 3) publish migration guide with cookbook examples and code snippets; 4) after 6 weeks of opt-in telemetry, flip the default for Dedicated customers then Hosted.
testing_plan: Unit tests in each language for framing decode/encode, interop tests that replay recorded streams (legacy + compact), end-to-end tests against mock runtime, load test for CBOR vs JSON modes, compatibility matrix against older SDK versions.
rollout_plan: 1) feature-flagged SDK release (alpha) with opt-in examples; 2) customer beta with Dedicated customers (2 weeks); 3) telemetry collection and bugfixes (4 weeks); 4) flip default for Hosted and document deprecation of legacy-only helpers.
acceptance_criteria: - TS/Py/Go shims pass interop suite; - migration guide published; - PR merged and CI green; - no regressions in per-token latency >5% in default JSON mode; - successful beta with at least 3 customers using compact mode.
